_readme: Deadlines the season check cannot discover for itself: they are facts about
accounts only their owner can see. Each entry is {what, due, note}.
`due` is a date in quotes — "2027-07-22" is the tidiest form, and anything
a date parser recognises works too, so "July 22, 2027" is fine. It must be
quoted: JSON has no bare dates, and an unquoted one makes the whole file
unreadable rather than just that row. `npm run check` catches that now.
null means 'not filled in yet' and makes the check nag gently. When one is
dealt with, move its due forward a year and the probe goes quiet on its own.
The check warns from 60 days out and fails once the date has passed.

deadlines.note: The renewal date is on https://developer.apple.com/account under Membership details. A lapse removes the app from the App Store outright.

deadlines.what: Google Play target API level review
deadlines.note: Google ratchets the required target API level yearly, with deadlines usually at the end of August — https://developer.android.com/google/play/requirements/target-sdk says the current one. Falling behind first hides the app from new users on current Android. The fix is the annual maintenance release: bump targetSdkVersion, build, submit.

Only applies once an upload keystore exists — it is generated when you first sign an Android release, not before, so leave this null until then. After that: a yearly reminder to confirm it is still in both places it should be (the ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 repository secret and an offline copy). It is the one secret here that cannot be reissued — Apple certificates reissue and Play can reset an upload key, but a lost keystore ends that app's update path for good.
